Neurodevelopmental disorder with developmental delay in 6/7; ptosis is 2/7 and individual renal and other ocular abnormalities are below 30%.

Congenital atrial septal defect; additional reported abnormalities also involve the cardiovascular axis.
Brucella infection; myalgia and arthralgia alone do not establish tissue damage, and destructive focal involvement is not consistently present in at least 30%.

Carcinoma arising in the intrahepatic canals of Hering; bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.

Cerebellar dysplastic gangliocytoma; extracerebral HPO findings reflect associated syndromes such as Cowden syndrome, not direct damage by the cerebellar lesion.

Catalase enzyme deficiency; oral ulceration occurs in 30-79%. Reduced erythrocyte enzyme activity alone is not blood-cell damage; anemia is occasional.
Acquired alpha-thalassemia with myelodysplastic marrow disease and cytopenias; dyspnea does not establish pulmonary damage.

Immune-complex small-vessel vasculitis; cutaneous vasculitic purpura affects most (>70%). Renal and nerve damage are less consistent in type III.

Congenital contractures and characteristic ptosis (7/10) define the syndrome; tongue atrophy directly affects oral tissue in 7/7.
Congenital ureteral duplication; ureters belong to the renal axis.
Endocrine growth disorder from deficient ghrelin-receptor signaling; delayed skeletal maturation and short stature do not establish skeletal damage.
Skin mastocytosis, hearing loss and microcephaly define syndrome; ID 2/3. Optic atrophy 80-99%; scoliosis 2/3 and contractures omitted under cap.
